disorder-name.detail: Amyloid-positive Alzheimer's Disease spectrum (ADS) cohort spanning preclinical AD (CDR=0, amyloid+; N=305), very mild dementia (CDR=0.5; N=236), and mild or more severe dementia (CDR>=1; N=185). Total N=726. The NM was applied to the entire ADS cohort as a single clinical group.
disorder-name.supporting_text: "a disease cohort of 726 amyloid positive AD spectrum (ADS) individuals across the following AD stages: preclinical stage with no symptoms (CDR = 0, A+)(N = 305), (b) CDR = 0.5(N = 236) and (c) CDR >= 1(N = 185)."
disorder-name.location: Kumar2024.pdf.md: Experimental set-up / Data and feature preprocessing, L191

dataset-of-origin.detail: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset. Both healthy controls and ADS cohort were drawn from ADNI.
dataset-of-origin.supporting_text: "we selected 248 cognitively unimpaired (healthy control) subjects from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging (ADNI) dataset Mueller et al., 2005"
dataset-of-origin.location: Kumar2024.pdf.md: Experimental set-up / Data and feature preprocessing, L189

age.detail: Age statistics for the ADS clinical cohort are not reported in the main paper. The age range for the model's one-hot encoding covers 47-91 years (from supplementary methods), but this reflects the encoding range, not the ADS cohort demographics specifically.
age.supporting_text: "each subject had an age vector with 44 positions, where each position corresponds to a year within the range of 47–91 years."

sex.detail: Sex distribution for the ADS clinical cohort (N=726) is not reported in the main paper. The model conditions on sex as a covariate but does not provide the breakdown for the disease cohort.
sex.supporting_text: "We conditioned our model on the age and sex of patients, represented as one-hot encoding vectors, to remove the effects of covariates from the MRI and PET features."
sex.location: Kumar2024.pdf.md: Experimental set-up / Data and feature preprocessing, L193
